chapter: Louis Armstrong, Basie and New York studio scene
title: Joe Glaser books Taylor's trio; the Hickory House and Basin Street West in 1954
summary: Taylor explains how Glaser's office got his trio a tour from the Hickory House, and they recall the downstairs Basin Street West on 51st Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: He was so funny though. The way I got him to book my trio was that I had been working at the Hickory House and I had gotten myself that job. But you know in those days I stayed on the job. I would go in for two weeks and stay for two years. So I was doing all right and John Popkin didn‟t care as long the people came in and bought some drinks, he was cool. So Joe Glazier sent a couple of his guys in to see me and say look we want to book you. So they got me a tour. So I am in Detroit and I am in Cleveland and in Chicago and everything. They have got a little circle for me, just to get me out of that room.
That was a great room there.
Joe Marcellus played there and Adele Jarod.
Yeah, that was a great room to play.
Yeah the bandstand was up over the bar.
Now were you working with Louie when he played the original Basin Street? Marty Kay opened up Basin Street, before Basin Street East. It was down on 50th Street.
Yeah 51st Street, downstairs. That was Basin Street West, yeah I was there.
And they had, if I remember correctly it was Louie and a woman who danced with a snake, or something, Soretta or something.
No I don‟t remember that. But I played that in 1954.
Now did they have one or two rooms?

Then that was later. We opened a room and the first concept of Basin Street was that the room was supposed to look like Basin Street. So you come downstairs and they have got a lamp post and a guy walking around with a guitar. But then they had a room off to the side and they had trios in there. And they had [Unintelligible] and my trio. And it was the weirdest bill I have ever been on. These cats in the trio, they were reading music and I am saying what is he reading. So I looked at his book between sets and it was lead sheets and stuff. Anyway, in the other room was Louie and he was…I never enjoyed Louie more because it was a night club and he would play like two or three shows a night. And man Louie was burning.
